inputs.subject: Internal Financial Materials: Riverfront Logistics CAC & LTV Narrative
inputs.body:
Here is the framework and narrative assistance for Riverfront Logistics' internal financial materials:

Current Financial Snapshot:
- Cash on Hand: $1.5M
- Runway: 6 months (Note: At a $72K/month burn rate, $1.5M would typically imply ~20 months of runway. You may want to clarify if the 6-month runway accounts for upcoming large capital expenditures, debt repayments, or projected burn increases to ensure the narrative is airtight).
- Burn Rate: $72K/month
- Last Quarter Revenue: $1.8M

Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) & Lifetime Value (LTV) Framework:

1. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
Formula: Total Sales & Marketing Expenses (over a specific period) / Number of New Customers Acquired (in that same period).
Narrative: Show how efficiently Riverfront Logistics is acquiring customers. If your CAC is decreasing over time, highlight this as a sign of scaling efficiency and strong market fit.

2. Lifetime Value (LTV)
Formula: Average Revenue Per Account (ARPA) × Gross Margin × Average Customer Lifespan.
Narrative: Emphasize the long-term value of your logistics contracts. High retention rates and recurring revenue from logistics clients will drive this number up.

3. The LTV:CAC Ratio
Target: The gold standard is 3:1 (meaning a customer brings in 3x what it costs to acquire them). 
Narrative: Tie this back to your strong quarterly revenue ($1.8M). If your LTV:CAC ratio is healthy, it proves that pouring more capital into the business will yield highly profitable growth, which perfectly sets up any conversations around extending that 6-month runway.

Let me know if you have the specific sales/marketing spend and customer numbers, and we can calculate the exact figures!
